content:
@George H. Seelinger (University of Michigan, Combinatorics Postdoc) and
I (Industry Mathematician) wanted to introduce ourselves and our pull
request #36698.

As an exercise, we started formalizing Latin Squares. These are a
classical combinatorics gadget and a starting point for the whole
theory of combinatorial designs. We noticed there isn't that much
combinatorics in Mathlib yet, but did notice Hall's Marriage theorem.

The main theorem this pull request proves is an application of Hall's
Marriage theorem: every Latin Rectangle extends to a Latin Square.

We wanted to prove an honest theorem instead of just formalizing data
structures and so we hope and believe this meets the bar!

Any feedback / thoughts on this pull request would be greatly
appreciated. In particular, we proved a tortured set-theoretic result
(count_by_group_or_element_indicator) that we believe may already
essentially be in Mathlib or at the very least should be placed in
another file. Another lemma we hope already exists is what we were
calling the unique_missed_element lemma.

Mathlib is an awesome project and we are excited to contribute.

Thanks again for any feedback!

Many of these proofs can be significantly golfed down, I picked some random snippets and golfed them a bit. I think this PR is quite long, especially for a new contributor PR. I'd suggest breaking out count_by_group_or_element_indicator/exists_larger_subset as a separate PR (probably living in some file about Finsets) to make it easier to review and marking the original as a dependent PR for now. I'd also take a look at the mathlib style and naming docs, in particular the names above don't mach mathlib conventions. I'd also try to really significantly golf these down, I wouldn't be surprised if these two could be reduced from ~200 lines to ~40.
I took a quick look and didn't see an immediate way to derive these 2 lemmas from whats in mathlib already, but I mostly focused on the syntactic-side

Vlad Tsyrklevich said:

(probably living in some file about Finsets)

I suggest Algebra/BigOperators/Group/Finset/Basic.lean, next to similar theorems

Thanks Vlad and Snir. I just merged in your improvements to the pull request.

We will factor out those set theory lemmas into their own pull request as you recommend and mark this one as dependent for now. Will improve the naming and try and shorten the proofs. Thanks again for the feedback!

Hey @Vlad Tsyrklevich and @Snir Broshi with your encouragement we shortened our proof of count_by_group_or_element_indicator (now named sum_card_eq_sum_card_fiber_biUnion) to 18 lines. This was done by reducing it to a combinatorics double theorem on bipartite graphs (Finset.sum_card_bipartiteAbove_eq_sum_card_bipartiteBelow). This made me realize that this result is a little more nuanced than I originally thought and so probably does not belong in the Finset.Basic file. Do you think this would make sense as a stand alone PR in a (yet to be determined) combinatorics file? I am thinking it could be PR'd into Mathlib.Combinatorics.Enumerative.DoubleCounting right below Finset.sum_card_bipartiteAbove_eq_sum_card_bipartiteBelow . Thanks for your thoughts!

Nice golf! I left a few small comments on it.

I think it makes sense as a standalone PR, perhaps with the following lemma in that file? Small self-contained PRs make reviews easier and it's normal to submit PRs with even just a single lemma--I'd guess that the average PR contains just a handful of new lemmas.

As far as placement, I'm not so familiar with this part of the library. If no one comes around with a different suggestion, I'd say just open it and let the reviewers decide if they think it should be placed elsewhere.

Hey @Vlad Tsyrklevich, thank you again for all the feedback! We have gone ahead and created a new PR for these two lemma results: #37190. When we separated them out, we also realized we could generalize them a little bit, so we implemented them slightly more generally. Next we will mark the Latin Square PR as dependent and continue working through your and others' comments.
